passage:
Class teacher's note on stream forms. Hansa handed in the commerce form on the same day as Arohi and four others. When I asked why, Hansa said, "We've always done everything together, so it's easier." Earlier Hansa had told me quietly that biology interests Hansa more than accounts. Arohi told me separately that Arohi would have been happy for Hansa to choose differently. I did not push. I asked Hansa to write two lines on what Hansa wants from each stream and to keep the form for a night. I also said that timetables change friendships whichever stream anyone picks. Hansa took the form home.
- Class teacher

qa.q: Which stream's form did Hansa hand in?
qa.a: Hansa handed in the commerce form.

qa.q: What does Hansa's remark about doing everything together suggest about Hansa's motive?
qa.a: That Hansa wants to stay with the group and avoid being left out, even though biology interests Hansa more.

qa.q: What would you advise Hansa to do with the form?
qa.a: Write down what Hansa wants from each stream and choose from that, remembering that friendships change anyway, so no one can be blamed for it later.

qa.q: How might Arohi see Hansa's choice?
qa.a: Arohi said privately that Arohi would have been happy for Hansa to choose differently, so Arohi may not have expected Hansa to follow for the group's sake.

grounding: Hansa follows the group into one stream to stay together; the teacher's note shows a different private interest and a nudge to choose independently.

passage:
In Class 10, our group of five did everything together: tuition, lunch, cricket on Sundays. When stream selection came, Tejas said, "PCM, all of us, obviously. Same class, same tuition." Everyone nodded. So did I, even though I'm Reena and I'd been drawing buildings in the margins of my notebooks for years.

I filled PCM. For the first three weeks of Class 11, I sat in physics feeling like I was drowning in a language I didn't speak. And the funny thing? The group was already splitting. Tejas was in a different section. Two of them joined a different tuition.

One night I realised I was about to spend two years in a stream I didn't want, for friends who were drifting anyway. And if I stayed, I'd blame them for it later.

I went to the office the next morning and switched to humanities with maths. I told the group at lunch. Tejas said, "Traitor," but he was grinning. We still play cricket on Sundays.

qa.q: What did Reena draw in the margins of notebooks?
qa.a: Reena drew buildings in the margins of notebooks.

qa.q: What was Reena feeling in physics during the first weeks of Class 11?
qa.a: Reena felt lost and overwhelmed, like drowning in a language Reena did not speak.

qa.q: What did Reena notice that helped make a better choice?
qa.a: Reena noticed the group was splitting anyway, so following them would mean regret and blame later, and chose humanities with maths instead.

qa.q: How does Tejas seem to see Reena's switch?
qa.a: Tejas teases Reena as a traitor but is grinning, which suggests he is not really upset and the friendship holds.

grounding: It shows a teen who follows friends into the same stream, notices the friendships are changing anyway and chooses for themselves before regret sets in.

passage:
Career counsellor's note, Class 10, stream choice week

Baljeet came to fill in his form with three friends, including Tushar. All four wrote "Science (PCM)." Baljeet's pen hovered for a long time before he wrote it.

I asked him to stay back. He said, "We've been together since nursery. If I take commerce, I'll be alone in a new section." When I asked about his marks, he said his best subjects are accounts and economics, and physics is his weakest.

I asked him to picture the day two years from now when he is stuck in a subject he doesn't like. Would he blame his friends? He said, "Probably. That's not fair on them, is it?"

We talked about how groups change after Class 10 anyway, new sections, new tuitions, new friends.

He came back the next day and asked for a new form. He wrote "Commerce." Tushar came with him and said, "We'll still have lunch, idiot." Baljeet laughed. I have noted his change in the office register.

qa.q: How many friends came with Baljeet to fill in the form?
qa.a: Baljeet came with three friends, including Tushar.

qa.q: What was Baljeet worried about as his pen hovered?
qa.a: Baljeet was anxious about being alone in a new section and losing his friends if he chose commerce.

qa.q: How did the counsellor help Baljeet choose for himself?
qa.a: The counsellor asked him to picture being stuck in a subject he disliked and whether he would blame his friends, which helped him see the real cost.

qa.q: How does Tushar see Baljeet's change of stream?
qa.a: Tushar seems supportive and relaxed about it, joking that they will still have lunch together.

grounding: It shows a teen following friends into one stream to stay together, then seeing that groups change anyway and choosing for himself to avoid regret later.
